about: Jim Halpert Pointing to Whiteboard is a two-panel image from The Office. In the top panel Jim, played by John Krasinski, stands beside an empty whiteboard on an easel, pointing at it with a marker and looking at the camera with a slight frown, mid-explanation. In the bottom panel the whiteboard is still blank and Jim smiles smugly at the camera, as if he has just made an unbeatable point. Users fill both boards with text, usually a statement or opinion followed by its supposed proof. The smug look lets it carry wholesome affirmations and sly trolling equally well.
origin: The frames come from The Office episode "Baby Shower" (season 5, 2008), in which Jim explains a plan on a whiteboard. Fans later blanked out the boards, and it became a popular two-panel edit format.
usage:
Write the first statement on the top whiteboard and the follow-up on the bottom one. The top usually states an opinion or rule; the bottom backs it up, twists it, or delivers a reassuring or cheeky conclusion as Jim smirks.

It is great for hot takes, wholesome reminders and self-justifying logic. Keep each board to one sentence so the text stays readable on the small whiteboard area.
